article.name: Helm
article.summary: Helm is a self-hosted personal agent with structured memory in a local SQLite database. Its facts and conversation episodes are written through a CLI and tool wrappers, recalled using BM25 fused with TF-IDF cosine or cached local MiniLM embeddings, and maintained through periodic reflection and consolidation. This is a source review, not a runtime or benchmark result.

who_what.text: The official README presents Helm as an open-source personal agent that runs on the user's hardware and connects to Discord, with optional iMessage and terminal surfaces.

The reviewed structured memory component is a Node workspace module backed by SQLite; the README also describes a separate Helm Mind Markdown knowledge base whose implementation was outside this review.

architecture.text: The structured memory database has facts, episodes, and links tables. Active facts are unique by (kind, key); facts carry confidence and lifecycle timestamps, episodes carry channel and raw_ref, and optional vectors are stored in separate tables.

CLI operations are wrapped by registered remember and recall tools. A generated Markdown index exposes selected facts and recent episodes to the agent context, while periodic think runs can invoke weekly consolidation.

behavior.text: remember inserts a fact, reinforces an identical value in place, or expires the old row and inserts a replacement when the value changes. Observed preferences receive a capped first confidence and repeated observations can raise the cap; this is bookkeeping, not independent verification.

Episodes append timestamped summaries with optional channel and raw_ref. Weekly consolidation derives learned terms from recurrent episode vocabulary, decays stale single-evidence facts, prunes below-floor rows except CLAUDE.md-sourced facts, and deduplicates active rows.

forget hard-deletes an individual fact and attempts to remove its fact vector; it does not expose episode deletion. Changed values remain in expired history, and erasure from side files, journals, or backups was not established.

Recall ranks up to 500 recently updated active facts with BM25 and cosine similarity, fusing ranks with reciprocal-rank fusion plus confidence and key-match boosts. Cosine uses cached MiniLM vectors only when the model is already available; otherwise the code uses TF-IDF, and embedding failures are silently caught.

Optional episode recall separately ranks up to 500 recent episodes by lexical and optional embedding similarity, weighted by recency. There is no explicit fact-answer abstention threshold in the inspected recall path.

metrics.evidence: Fact and optional episode ranking were inspected; no answerability or abstention workload was scored.
Value supersession and history retention were inspected; no correction probes were run.
A fact delete path exists but episode deletion and complete-copy erasure were not established; no post-delete probes were run.
The database schema has no principal/project key and the Discord owner gate is outside the store; no cross-scope workload was run.
Source labels and evidence counters were inspected; no response claims were adjudicated against stored passages.
SQLite and optional local embeddings were inspected; no token, cost, or persistent storage measurements were collected.

limits.text: The structured memory CLI has facts, episodes and lifecycle metadata, but the inspected API does not establish per-user, project, or tenant isolation inside the store.

The confidence and evidence counters are application-maintained signals; observed repeats are not checked for independence or truth, and arbitrary confidence input is not range-validated in the inspected remember path.
Fact deletion is available, but episode deletion and complete erasure from database journals, indexes, backups, or other copies remain unknown from the reviewed paths.
The reviewed product README's privacy and capability statements are upstream claims; this source review did not test them. Helm Mind details and measured runtime behavior were not examined.

benchmark.note: No Helm runtime, tests, or benchmark workload was run. Code observations and project evaluation definitions are not Helm benchmark results.
